|url-status=dead |archive-date=June 21, 2019 |access-date=June 21, 2019}} ==College career== A native of [[Port St. Lucie, Florida]], James was an unheralded basketball recruit out of high school, generating only one high-major offer from [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State]], before ultimately going to the [[University of Wyoming]]. He became a full-time contributor by his sophomore year and increased his scoring average each year.{{cite news |last=Potter |first=Davis |title=Justin James' passion, production sold the Sacramento Kings on him |work=[[Casper Star-Tribune]] |date=June 21, 2019 |url=https://trib.com/sports/college/wyoming/mbb/justin-james-passion-production-sold-the-sacramento-kings-on-him/article_3505ac86-4a53-5071-a7f1-1cc9fc43ef13.html |access-date=June 22, 2019}} James led the [[Mountain West Conference]] in scoring during his final season at Wyoming, averaging 22.1 points per game as a senior, despite playing as a point guard, a position he does not normally play, because Wyoming needed James to have the ball as much as possible during an 8–24 season. He also led the Cowboys with 8.5 rebounds and 4.4 assists per game, and made second-team All-Mountain West. James had a three-point field goal percentage of 33.7 percent during his college career. Despite his high scoring, James posted career lows in field goal percentage (40.9 percent) and three-point field goal percentage (29.6 percent) during his senior high, as well as 4.1 turnovers per game. James finished his college career with 2,061 points, the third highest in Mountain West history. He also participated in the [[Portsmouth Invitational Tournament]], one of 64 seniors from around the country invited to the event.{{cite news |last=Nowlin |first=Jack |date=April 16, 2019 |title=Wyoming's Justin James will play in Portsmouth Invitational Tournament |work=[[Casper Star-Tribune]] |url=https://trib.com/sports/college/wyoming/mbb/wyoming-s-justin-james-will-play-in-portsmouth-invitational-tournament/article_fd5bd20a-dfd1-5150-a7c2-3594389c0dd7.html |access-date=June 21, 2019}} ==Professional career== ===Sacramento Kings (2019–2021)=== James was selected by the [[Sacramento Kings]] in the second round of the [[2019 NBA draft]] with the 40th overall pick, and became the first University of Wyoming player drafted since the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] selected [[Larry Nance Jr.]] in 2015. [[CBS Sports]] had ranked James as the 96th-best prospect heading into the draft, while the ''[[Sporting News]]'' and NBADraft.net had him unranked, and most [[mock draft]]s did not predict he would be picked. Sacramento general manager [[Vlade Divac]] said the team drafted him because they followed his college career and appreciated his passion and production: "We talked to everybody about his professionalism and his love for the game. We were so excited when we spent time with him in Sacramento." On July 10, 2019, the [[Sacramento Kings]] announced that they had signed James.{{cite web|title=Kings Sign Justin James|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-justin-james|date=July 10, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 10, 2019}} On October 25, 2019, James made his debut in the NBA, coming off the bench in a 112–122 loss to the [[2019–20 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland Trail Blazers]] with two points.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160666|title=Lillard scores 35 as Trail Blazers top Kings 122-112|date=October 25, 2019|website=ESPN.com|access-date=October 25, 2019}} He scored 30 points for the [[G League]]'s [[Stockton Kings]] in a win over the [[Iowa Wolves]] on January 11, 2020.{{cite news |title=Kings' Justin James: Scores 30 points in G League win |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/kings-justin-james-scores-30-points-in-g-league-win/ |access-date=January 13, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 12, 2020}} ===Cleveland Charge (2021–2022)=== On September 22, 2021, James signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web |last=Adams |first=Luke |date=September 22, 2021 |title=Jazz Sign Justin James To Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/09/jazz-sign-justin-james-to-two-way-contract.html |access-date=December 17, 2023 |website=HoopsRumors.com}} However, he was waived on October 1.{{cite web |last=Chunga |first=JP |date=October 1, 2021 |title=Utah Jazz Waive Justin James |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-waive-justin-james |access-date=October 3, 2021 |website=NBA.com}} On October 13, he signed with [[Cleveland Cavaliers]],{{cite web |last=Gold |first=Matthew |date=October 13, 2021 |title=Cavaliers Sign Ed Davis |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/davis-signing-211013 |access-date=October 23, 2021 |website=NBA.com}} but was waived three days later.{{cite web |last=Georgia |date=October 16, 2021 |title=Cavaliers Convert the Contracts of Tacko Fall and RJ Nembhard into Two-way Contracts |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/cavaliers-convert-contracts-tacko-fall-and-rj-nembhard-two-way-contracts |access-date=October 23, 2021 |website=NBA.com}} On October 23, he signed with the [[Cleveland Charge]] as an affiliate player.{{cite web|title=Cleveland Charge 2021-22 Training Camp Roster|url=https://canton.gleague.nba.com/news/cleveland-charge-2021-22-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} James averaged 17.8 points, 4.8 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game. On December 26, 2021, the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] signed James to a 10-day contract.{{cite web|title=Pelicans sign Anthony Tolliver and Justin James to 10-day contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-anthony-tolliver-and-justin-james-10-day-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=December 26, 2021|access-date=December 27, 2021}} However, he never appeared in a game for the team. On January 5, 2022, James was reacquired by the Cleveland Charge.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League transactions|date=January 5, 2022|access-date=January 5, 2022}} James joined the [[Orlando Magic]] for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web |title=Orlando Magic 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612753/magic |access-date=July 5, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} === Metropolitans 92 (2022–2023) === On December 13, 2022, James signed with [[Metropolitans 92]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.metropolitans92.com/fr/actualites/2022-12-13/justin-james-pigiste-medical-pour-aaron-henry|title=Justin JAMES, pigiste médical pour Aaron HENRY|last=|first=|date=December 13, 2022|website=metropolitans92.com|publisher=|language=fr|access-date=December 13, 2022}} === Return to the Charge (2023) === On March 2, 2023, James was re-acquired by the [[Cleveland Charge]].{{Cite web |date=March 3, 2023 |title=Charge Acquire Justin James |url=https://cleveland.gleague.nba.com/news/charge-acquire-justin-james |access-date=March 2, 2023 |website=Cleveland Charge}} === Álftanes (2024–2025) === On 16 December 2024, James signed with [[Álftanes (men's basketball)|Álftanes]] of the Icelandic [[Úrvalsdeild karla (basketball)|Úrvalsdeild karla]].{{cite news |title=Reyndur NBA-leikmaður til Álftaness |url=https://www.mbl.is/sport/korfubolti/2024/12/16/reyndur_nba_leikmadur_til_alftaness/ |access-date=17 December 2024 |work=[[Morgunblaðið]] |date=16 December 2024 |language=is}} On 31 January, he scored a season-high 34 points in a win against [[ÍR (men's basketball)|ÍR]]. During the regular season he averaged a team-high 23.1 points along with 5.4 rebounds and 4.0 assists. In the playoffs, he helped Álftanes reach the semi-finals where they bowed out against [[Tindastóll (men's basketball)|Tindastóll]]. In eight playoff games, he averaged 24.0 points, 7.3 rebounds and 5.3 assists.{{cite web |title=Justin James |url=https://kki.is/motamal/leikir-og-urslit/motayfirlit/Leikmadur?league_id=undefined&season_id=128582&player_id=6895044 |access-date=August 2, 2025 |website=kki.is |publisher=[[Icelandic Basketball Association]] |language=is}} === Kaohsiung Aquas (2025) === On August 2, 2025, James signed with the [[Kaohsiung Aquas]] of the [[Taiwan Professional Basketball League]] (TPBL).{{cite news |title=高雄海神簽下前NBA搖擺人詹姆斯 曾與溫班亞瑪當隊友 |url=https://sports.ettoday.net/news/3007967 |access-date=August 2, 2025 |work=ETtoday |date=August 2, 2025 }} On November 10, Kaohsiung Aquas terminated the contract relationship with James.{{cite web |title=Thank you JJ |url=https://www.facebook.com/ktown.aquas/posts/1150425320629516 |website=Facebook |publisher=高雄全家海神隊 Kaohsiung Aquas |date=November 10, 2025
